markdown:
# Product foundation

## Product
Chaser sends polite payment reminders for freelance designers so they stop chasing late invoices by hand. Chaser is a working name, not fixed.

## Problem
Freelance designers chase late invoices by hand. They keep a spreadsheet and write awkward emails weeks after the due date, or let it slide. They lose a few hours a month on it. Their invoices come from a tool like Wave or from a PDF.

## Persona
A freelance brand or web designer working alone, with 3 to 10 active clients. They invoice from a tool like Wave or a PDF. They want the money without having to ask for it. What stops them: they hate asking for money.

## Core scenario
On a Monday morning at their desk, on a laptop, a designer sees an invoice is two weeks overdue. They hand it to Chaser in under a minute and do not think about it again until the money lands. This happens a few times a month. Done means the invoice is with Chaser and the designer has nothing left to do.

## Also affected
The designer's clients, who get the reminders. They should feel nudged, not accused.

## Not for
Agencies with a finance person.

## Feel
Calm, friendly, a bit dry. Never pushy, corporate or cute.

## Goals
1. 50 paying users by the end of March 2027.

Earns by: See Open.

## Anti-goals
1. We will not build invoicing itself.
2. No mobile app.

## Assumptions
- Designers will let a tool email their clients in their name.

## Open
- Core scenario: how the designer hands an invoice to Chaser is not said (a Wave link, a PDF upload, or something else).
- Goals: "Grow fast after that" has no number and no date.
- Goals: Earns by is empty. No price or way of earning is said, so "paying users" has no meaning yet.
- Anti-goals: neither item says why we will not build it.
- Assumptions: nothing says how we will test whether designers accept emails sent in their name.

questions.question: How does the designer hand an invoice to Chaser: paste a Wave link, upload a PDF, or forward an email?
questions.why: The one-minute handoff is the whole scenario, and each route implies a different user, tool and build.

questions.question: Does "Agencies with a finance person" turn away a solo designer who has a bookkeeper or a part-time assistant?
questions.why: The line is vague about who counts as an agency, so it may refuse signups the persona would accept.
options: Solo only, any helper is out

questions.question: Can a client tell who sent the reminder, and can they reply or mark the invoice paid?
questions.why: Clients feel the tone, and a reminder in the designer's name that cannot be answered may read as an accusation.
options: Reply or paid link in email

questions.question: How does Chaser earn money, and at what price?
questions.why: "Paying users" in goal 1 means nothing until there is a price or way of earning, so the March 2027 count cannot be checked.

questions.question: What counts as a paying user on the date: anyone who has paid once, or someone paying that month?
questions.why: The check on 31 March 2027 gives a different number under each reading, and a trial-to-paid rule would change the goal itself.

questions.question: Should the goal also say how much of the late money Chaser gets back, or is sign-ups alone enough?
questions.why: 50 paying users can be reached while reminders fail to collect, and a recovery number would pull against the 'polite, never pushy' feel.

questions.question: Why will Chaser not build invoicing, given that it must read invoices from Wave or PDFs anyway?
questions.why: Without a reason, a feature like "create an invoice to chase" cannot be judged as in or out.
options: Wave and PDFs already do it

questions.question: Should Chaser ever escalate to firm or legal-sounding demands for payment on a very late invoice?
questions.why: Escalation is the obvious next feature for a chaser and it could break the promise that clients feel nudged, not accused.

questions.question: Will Chaser ever take or hold the client's payment, for example with a pay-now link in the reminder?
questions.why: A pay link is a tempting add-on that brings money handling and rules, and the document says nothing on it.
options: Link to their own invoice only

questions.question: What evidence do you have that designers lose real time or money to late invoices, and that they would pay to fix it?
questions.why: The Problem is asserted with no proof; "a few hours a month" is a guess, and if it is false the product has no buyer.

questions.question: Would designers let a tool email their clients in their own name, and how will you find out before building?
questions.why: This is the one assumption that ends the product if false, and the document has no test for it.

questions.question: What do designers use today to chase invoices, and why would they switch to Chaser?
questions.why: Wave and similar invoice tools already send automatic reminders, so the document must say what Chaser does that they and a spreadsheet do not.
